task_message:
Case N03: segment the peripheral nerve sheath tumor on this T2-weighted MRI.

Volume: 151x151x165 voxels, 1 mm isotropic. Budgets: max 40 tool calls / 15 model prompts / 10 min wall time.
Start with `seg_open`. Finish with `seg_finish`.
final_assistant_text:
Case N03 is complete. 

**Final result:** a single 2.4 mL mask of the peripheral nerve sheath tumor in the posterior compartment, spanning axial 61–82 (≈22 mm), coronal 55–68 (≈13 mm) and sagittal 61–78 (≈17 mm).

**Workflow summary:**
1. Scanned the volume in axial, coronal and sagittal sheets; identified the hyperintense, slightly lobulated nodule in the posterior compartment on T2.
2. Seeded the model with two positive points (marks 81 and 426) on the lesion core — initial mask v1 (2.4 mL) already matched the bright mass well in all three planes.
3. Verified the boundary with zoomed mask views in axial, coronal and sagittal planes, checked the ends (axial 56, 60, 84, 88, 97) for tumor continuation.
4. Ran `seg_refine`, which produced essentially no change (stable boundary, v2).
5. Evaluated the automatic candidates C1/C2 (a thin bright streak extending superiorly from the mass): accepted, inspected, and reverted — its intermediate intensity and linear, tapering course fit the parent nerve/peritumoral edema rather than tumor, so it was excluded (checked out v2).
6. Final review showed the outline following the lesion in all five slices per plane, no lesion tissue beyond the mask ends and no stray components.

Confidence is medium because the small equivocal superior streak could conceivably represent tumor extension along the nerve.
